acceptance: TestRun_StopSignalEndsRunAndClosesFile sends the stop from the reader after a counted read and has no time.Sleep
fix: Make the stop depend on counted reads, not on a sleep. The test wraps fakeReader in a reader that sends SIGTERM on the stop channel when it serves its Nth read (N large enough for at least one sample, given that a CPU percent needs two readings), and the test asserts at least one sample. Keep the 80ms sleep out of the test. Red first: a reader that sends the stop on its first read makes the current assertion fail, which proves that the test depends on the order of reads and stop.
summary: Main CI run 44781012877 on b2884a911 (2026-11-20) failed in the macOS darwin set on go/cmd/hostsampler TestRun_StopSignalEndsRunAndClosesFile with main_test.go:83 'no samples' after 0.11s. The next two main runs passed with no change to the package, so the test is flaky. The test (go/cmd/hostsampler/main_test.go:72-85) starts a goroutine that sleeps 80ms and then sends SIGTERM, and it expects at least one sample at a 10ms interval. Under -race on a loaded macOS runner, the run can receive the stop before it writes a sample, because the test synchronises on wall time and not on work that the sampler did.
title: the hostsampler stop test sends its signal after a sleep, so a loaded runner can stop the run before the first sample
